title: Finite limits of internal abelian groups are created on underlying objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. Write $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ for the category whose objects are quadruples $(M,m,e,i)$, with $m:M\times M\to M$, $e:*\to M$ and $i:M\to M$ satisfying associativity, commutativity, the two unit laws and the inverse laws as equations of morphisms; here $*$ is terminal and products have the meaning of [def-weil-category-product]. Morphisms preserve these operations. Let $U_{\mathcal C}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ forget the operations.

For every finite category $I$, every diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ and every limiting cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$ of $U_{\mathcal C}D$, there is exactly one abelian-group-object structure on the same object $L$ making all $p_j$ group-object morphisms. With this structure the cone is limiting in $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$: the unique underlying factorization of any group-object cone is a group-object morphism. Moreover, a cone of group objects is limiting if and only if its underlying cone is limiting. Thus $U_{\mathcal C}$ creates, preserves and reflects finite limits, including the empty limit.

Let $\mathcal D$ also have finite limits, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits. Equip $FM$ with $F(m)\circ\lambda_{M,M}^{-1}$, $F(e)\circ\lambda_*^{-1}$ and $F(i)$, where $\lambda_{M,N}:F(M\times N)\to FM\times FN$ and $\lambda_*:F(*)\to *$ are the canonical comparisons. This operation transport, with $h\mapsto F(h)$ on morphisms, defines a functor $F^{\mathrm{ab}}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal D)$, and $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ preserves finite limits.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Mon.limit to the diagram forgotten to internal monoids and the given underlying limit cone. Its explicit one and multiplication are the unique factorizations of their operation cones; its monoid laws hold by joint monicity of the limit projections. Form the inverse cone using GrpObj.inv_hom and diagram naturality, and factor it through the same underlying limit. After composition with each projection, lift_map_assoc and the component inverse laws give both inverse laws. Braiding naturality and the component commutativity law give commutativity. This constructs liftObject on exactly the given cone point, including for an empty diagram.

Construct liftCone using the monoid-limit projections, regarded as group morphisms and then commutative-group morphisms. The underlying cone is definitionally the original cone. Use Mon.limitConeIsLimit for the factorization of every cone, now regarded as a group morphism. The underlying limit equations prove factorization and uniqueness, giving liftConeIsLimit.

The composite of the fully faithful forgetful functors to groups and monoids with Mon.forget reflects isomorphisms. Apply createsLimitOfReflectsIso to liftCone, its literal underlying equality, and liftConeIsLimit. Package this as CreatesFiniteLimits. Its standard API gives preservation; reflection is obtained shape by shape from creation. Hence a group cone is limiting if and only if its forgotten cone is limiting.

For the strict unique-structure clause, use the constructed cone and group structure as witness. Given any competing structure, first substitute its underlying-object equality. Its projection homomorphisms and the constructed projection homomorphisms show equality of the two multiplication maps after every limit projection. Joint monicity gives equality of multiplication; MonObj.ext then identifies the monoid structures and GrpObj.ext identifies the group structures. Commutativity proofs are propositions, so the bundled objects and their subtype elements coincide.

For F preserving finite limits, equip it with Functor.Braided.ofChosenFiniteProducts and use the explicit Mathlib Functor.mapCommGrp construction. The underlying composite equality is reflexivity. Unfold the three transported operations: multiplication and unit are the lax monoidal comparison followed by F of the original operation, while inverse is F of inverse. Functor.Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory and ε_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory identify the first two comparisons with the inverses of prodComparisonIso and preservesTerminalIso. This verifies all three asserted operation equations.

Repeat finite-limit creation and reflection in the target category. The underlying composite of mapCommGrp with its forgetful functor is definitionally the original forgetful functor followed by F; this composite preserves finite limits. Apply preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves to infer preservation by mapCommGrp. All constructions and projection arguments include the empty limit.

A : { A : CommGrp C // A.X = c.pt }, (∀ j : I, ∃ f : A.val ⟶ D.obj j, eqToHom A.property.symm ≫ (forget C).map f = c.π.app j) ∧ ∃ s : Cone D, s.pt = A.val ∧ (forget C).mapCone s = c ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit s)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) [SmallCategory I] [FinCategory I] (D : I ⥤ CommGrp C) (c : Cone D), Nonempty (IsLimit c) ↔ Nonempty (IsLimit ((forget C).mapCone c))) ∧ Nonempty (CreatesFiniteLimits (forget C)) ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits (forget C) ∧ ReflectsFiniteLimits (forget C) ∧ (∀ (E : Type u') [Category.{v'} E] [HasFiniteLimits E] [CartesianMonoidalCategory E] [BraidedCategory E] (F : C ⥤ E) [PreservesFiniteLimits F], ∃ (H : CommGrp C ⥤ CommGrp E) (hH : H ⋙ forget E = forget C ⋙ F), (∀ A : CommGrp C, MonObj.mul (X := (H.obj A).X) ≫ (eqToIso hH).hom.app A = ((eqToIso hH).hom.app A ⊗ₘ (eqToIso hH).hom.app A) ≫ (prodComparisonIso F A.X A.X).inv ≫ F.map (MonObj.mul (X := A.X)) ∧ MonObj.one (X := (H.obj A).X) ≫ (eqToIso hH).hom.app A = (preservesTerminalIso F).inv ≫ F.map (MonObj.one (X := A.X)) ∧ GrpObj.inv (X := (H.obj A).X) ≫ (eqToIso hH).hom.app A = (eqToIso hH).hom.app A ≫ F.map (GrpObj.inv (X := A.X))) ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits H)
lean.note: Mathlib CommGrp is the existing internal abelian-group-object notion, written multiplicatively. CartesianMonoidalCategory and its unique braiding specify the chosen finite products, available for every finite-limit category; they impose no additional mathematical property. The first conjunct fixes the underlying limit object literally and supplies its lifted limiting cone. The final existential specifies the transported functor by strict underlying equality and all three canonical operation equations.
